qt: to the Commission Dick Erixon (ECR) Subject:

Rising interest costs risk making the EU an even greater burden on Member States and their citizens. The European Court of Auditors warns that outstanding EU borrowing could exceed EUR 900 billion by 20271. It also points out that interest on the NextGenerationEU recovery debt could cost around double the EUR 14.9 billion set aside for 2021-2027, and that interest rates rose significantly after the borrowing began. In early September 2026, government bond yields in Germany and France reached 15-year highs2. 1.
What is the Commission’s latest estimate of total NextGenerationEU interest costs, and how much higher is it than originally planned?
Does the Commission plan to cut other EU spending to cover these costs, so that neither taxes nor Member States’ contributions have to rise?

European Court of Auditors, ‘2024 EU audit in brief – Introducing the 2004 annual reports of the European Court of Auditors’, October 2025. 2 Euronews, ‘European government bond yields surge to 15-year highs as sell-off deepens’, 1 September 2026, https://www.euronews.com/business/2026/09/01/european-government-bond-yields-surge-to-15-yearhighs-as-sell-off-deepens. 1
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) According to the latest information included in the Amending Letter to the Draft Budget 20271, adopted by the Commission on 9 October 2026, the interest costs for NextGenerationEU (NGEU)2 non-repayable support (‘EURI costs’) to be charged to the 2027 budget amount to EUR 9.9 billion. This brings the total EURI costs over the 2021-2027 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) period to EUR 27.5 billion, which is EUR 12.6 billion higher than the EUR 14.9 billion originally planned. This increase is the result of the sharp increase in interest rates in the years since 2020, when the original estimates were set. Between 2021 and 2024 – when interest rate increases were not as severe – the additional needs (i.e. the funding costs which exceed the amounts initially programmed) for the financing of NGEU borrowing costs were met through existing allocations and the use of available budgetary flexibilities. Following the MFF mid-term revision3 and in line with the agreement reached on the application of the ‘EURI cascade mechanism’ in the Conciliation on the 2025 budget4, from 2025 onwards all additional funding costs, i.e. amounts above the originally planned amount, are financed as follows: a) 50% covered from existing budgetary availabilities and special instruments; b) 50% are covered by the new EURI Instrument, fully financed by decommitments made since 2021. As for the 2028-2034 MFF, the Commission proposal of 16 July 20255 foresees a fixed annual NGEU debt service amount of EUR 24 billion per year in current prices, covering both interest costs and capital repayment. The Commission considers that the proposed approach of a fixed annual debt service amount does not risk affecting other expenditures as with this approach, and under the current simulations, the liabilities from the NGEU would be fully repaid by 2058, as originally planned.
